title: Asymptotic analysis of a Fredholm determinant occurring in the description of the dynamical correlation functions of the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas
authors: Frank Göhmann, Karol K. Kozlowski, Mikhail D. Minin
abstract: We perform a large-$x$ asymptotic analysis of the Fredholm determinant of an integrable integral operator with generalized sine kernel, where $x$ controls the strength of the oscillations along the integration contour of the operator and will play the role of the distance variable in applications to the correlation functions of integrable quantum systems. Our generalized sine kernel involves a number of functional parameters that will allow us to adapt it to the analysis of the dynamical correlation functions of the Lieb--Liniger model at finite temperature and for all positive values of the coupling constant. It will also allow us to consider a class of equilibrium correlation functions that are governed by generalized Gibbs ensembles. Our work is based on the analysis of a matrix Riemann--Hilbert problem that is canonically connected with our integrable integral operator.
summary: This paper develops a sophisticated asymptotic analysis technique to evaluate Fredholm determinants arising from the Lieb-Liniger Bose gas. By mapping the problem onto a matrix Riemann-Hilbert problem, the authors derive precise large-$x$ expansions for correlation functions. This provides crucial theoretical tools for understanding quantum dynamics in integrable many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper performs a large-$x$ asymptotic analysis of a Fredholm determinant associated with an integrable integral operator.
main_result: It derives explicit asymptotic expansions for the Fredholm determinant, accounting for leading exponential decay, logarithmic corrections, and constant terms based on the location of poles.
method: The analysis is fundamentally based on solving a matrix Riemann-Hilbert problem using non-linear steepest descent methods and saddle-point approximations in the complex plane.
model_or_system: The context is the Lieb–Liniger Bose gas, allowing the calculation of its dynamical correlation functions at finite temperature. The mathematical machinery involves an integrable integral operator with a generalized sine kernel.
key_observables: Dynamical and equilibrium correlation functions; the Fredholm determinant $\det R (	ext{id} + V)$.
important_parameters:
The large parameter $x$ (acting as a distance variable), functional parameters ($u, \vartheta, g, 
u$), and temperature/coupling constant regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of saddle points ($\lambda_0$) and poles ($S$) in the complex plane, and involves systematic handling of residues from the RHP factorization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the integration contour $C_{\lambda_0}$ in the complex plane, define the Cauchy transform $C(\lambda)$, and sketch the behavior of exponential terms relative to the saddle point $\lambda_0$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the analysis by first establishing the connection between the Fredholm determinant and a matrix Riemann-Hilbert problem. It then applies asymptotic methods (steepest descent) based on the number of poles encountered in the complex plane.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful, rigorous mathematical tools for calculating correlation functions in integrable quantum systems, which is highly relevant to understanding non-equilibrium dynamics and thermalization in many-body physics.
